componentPlan.focusQuote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Maps central drag dependencies before detailing coefficients and areas.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of coefficient meaning, testing method and pressure ideas.

overview.headline: Drag forces and the drag equation in flight

keyPoints.point: Students learn that drag depends on air density and velocity with viscosity effects included.
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyPoints.point: Students learn how drag relates to drag coefficient, density, velocity and reference area.
keyPoints.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared

keyPoints.point: Students learn that drag coefficient combines form drag, friction drag and wave effects from tests.
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that reported drag values require a stated reference area for correct conversion.
keyPoints.quote: the aerodynamicist must specify the area used; when using the data, the reader may have to convert the drag coefficient

keyTerms.gloss: Aerodynamic force that depends on density and velocity
keyTerms.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyTerms.gloss: Main variable that collects complex drag effects into calculation
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: Chosen area basis used to characterize size dependence of drag
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: Air property designated by the letter rho
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: Combined density and velocity effect that appears in pressure relation
keyTerms.quote: is called the dynamic pressure and appears in Bernoulli’s pressure equation.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains what affects drag, how the drag coefficient collects complex effects, how reference area choices change the coefficient, and how density and dynamic pressure appear in the equation.
analysis.subject: physics
